correctness.rationale: For the specified finite-state continuous-time patch occupancy process, the Poisson transition rates yield a unique rational solution to the transient backward equations for each positive colonization rate. Four symbolic exact-polynomial Cramer cross-identities prove the quoted rational functions; two polynomial difference factorizations are checked exactly. Positive denominators and a one-sign-change degree-nine numerator give a unique positive crossing. Exact adjacency characteristic polynomials give spectral ordering. A complete graph isomorphism census through four nodes proves the first instance, and independent full-state rational arithmetic verifies the formulas at three sample rates.

A material-read gap for Frank is retained as risk rather than a claim of full noncoverage.

originality.rationale: The original contribution is narrow: the sharp matched-number-of-patches-and-links spectral-versus-stochastic ranking contradiction at four patches, a single exact colonization-rate crossing, and the smaller tree-stratum exclusion. Broad stochastic-versus-deterministic ranking disagreements are explicitly known from Frank (2005), and raw small-graph SIS exact times are broadly covered by Holme–Tupikina (2018). The examined sources and targeted alias/implication searches did not state the new cross-graph spectral ranking theorem; remaining risk is recorded.
residual_risks: Frank (2005) already establishes general stochastic-versus-deterministic persistence ranking changes. Its full paper could not be inspected; a specific paw/cycle example or implication in its body cannot be excluded on abstract evidence alone.

Holme–Tupikina (2018) already computed all small-graph SIS extinction-time functions. Although their published text does not give the present spectral comparison, an archived source-code dataset or unindexed appendix might contain the exact paw/cycle crossing.

The leading adjacency eigenvalue equals a spatially weighted landscape-capacity proxy only under equal-quality binary connectivity assumptions; the finding makes no universal statement for general heterogeneous metapopulation capacity.

value.rationale: The spectral landscape capacity proxy and finite stochastic mean persistence are conceptually important but nonidentical ecological measurements. Fixed patch and link budgets isolate topological effects relevant to a fair habitat-network comparison. The four-patch minimality theorem, exact one-rate crossover, and explicit rate-two ranking reversal give the earliest possible simple counterexample to substitution of spectral capacity for finite-stochastic persistence, with a transparent closed algebraic certificate rather than a table recomputation alone.
